records.content: FICTIONAL: Several member organisations rely on one or two donors and have limited documented fundraising plans.
FICTIONAL: Funding sources increased for one coastal member after a joint proposal, but the record has no comparable baseline.
FICTIONAL: Leaders described continuity risks when experienced programme managers leave.
FICTIONAL: Staff reported that local programme learning is often retained in personal files rather than shared systems.
FICTIONAL: Shared governance training improved confidence for some participants; attendance and application were not measured consistently.
FICTIONAL: Cross-member collaboration is stronger where existing relationships and regular peer meetings are present.
FICTIONAL: Donors valued joint proposals but requested clearer evidence of member capability and governance systems.
FICTIONAL: A locally successful youth programme was not transferred because its documentation was incomplete.
FICTIONAL: Community contributors valued locally adapted services and cautioned against copying another member's approach without consultation.
FICTIONAL: Digital capability varied substantially; some members used shared tools while others lacked reliable access.
FICTIONAL: A different member reported stable funding through local partners rather than pooled fundraising.
FICTIONAL: Staff described peer exchange as useful but reported that no shared learning calendar exists.
FICTIONAL: Some leaders favoured a shared service centre; others worried it could reduce local autonomy.
FICTIONAL: Leadership mentoring participation was high in one area and low in another due to travel schedules.
FICTIONAL: Joint proposal development was attempted by two members but outcomes were not recorded.
FICTIONAL: Documentation standards were absent from one monthly record.
